newsitem.title: UK: Shandwick sees adverse impact on H2 profit.
newsitem.headline: Shandwick sees adverse impact on H2 profit.

text.p: Shandwick Plc, the world's largest independent public relations firm, on Tuesday said problems in the UK and international investment are expected to adversely impact its second-half profits.

"In comparing our full-year results with 1996 we, like other multi-national companies reporting in sterling, will have absorbed a substantial adverse currency translation impact -- estimated at around nine million pounds ($14.7 million) on revenues and one million pounds on profits -- due to the strength of sterling," chairman Lord Chadlington said in a statement.

"While this has been anticipated since early in the year, problems in the UK and investment in the international account structure will now have some profit impact in the second half, which may be partly compensated by performance elsewhere in the world," Chadlington said.
But worldwide business is growing satisfactorily and double-digit fee revenue growth is expected to continue for the full year in constant currencies, he added.

Shandwick earlier on Tuesday reported first-half pre-tax profit rose to 3.9 million pounds from 3.6 million pounds in the 1996 first-half. Turnover rose to 89.6 million pounds from 87.8 million pounds.
Shandwick derives about 80 percent of its fees outside the UK.
Chief executive Dermot McNulty in a statement noted that the company's Americas region was the lead factor in Shandwick's double-digit revenue growth in the 1997 first half.
Revenue in Asia Pacific rose 5.9 percent in constant currencies in the first half, while falling 2.5 percent in Britain and 3.1 percent in continental Europe, McNulty said.
